1.why: All 14 screenshots show static, card-based pages with no animations, moving images, or pop-ups.

2.why: Primary actions are solid blue buttons, the active step is a filled pill, focused buttons get an orange ring, and confirmations appear in bold green, so important items clearly stand out.

3.why: A single-column layout with one task per screen makes fields and buttons easy to locate, although the codes the user needs sit in the Logs panel at the bottom of the page.

4.why: The visible stepper and 'Next:' banners externalize the steps and the password rules are printed above the fields, leaving little to remember, though the overall flow is long.

5.why: No 'remember me', autofill, or password-manager option appears on any sign-in or recovery screen.

6.why: Completed steps stay visible with green outlines and the persistent header and Logs let the user recognize progress, but no personalized saved items such as a username are shown.

7.why: Instructions are short, plain sentences like 'Enter your registered email address' and 'Use 12 or more characters with uppercase, lowercase, a number, and a symbol', with no dense paragraphs.

8.why: No error state appears in any screenshot, only green success messages, so whether error messages describe the problem and fix cannot be verified.

9.why: The email, code, and password fields show no placeholder examples or format hints; the only example-like guidance is 'Check for https://localhost' in the help text.

10.why: The authentication options that are presented (password sign-in, send/confirm security code, start recovery) are clearly labelled, though no alternative such as face login is offered.

11.why: Each screen offers at most one primary decision and two buttons (e.g. 'Send security code' / 'Confirm security code'), never presenting many choices at once.

12.why: Every action produces a bold green status line and a Logs entry (e.g. 'A security code has been prepared'), but the signed-out page keeps a stale 'Password confirmed' message.

13.why: Every screen shows the 'Help and safe sign-in reminders' panel plus a step-specific 'Next:' banner telling the user exactly what to do next.

14.why: The help text promises 'no page countdown' and the 'Forgot your password? Start recovery' link lets the user restart, though no actual error-and-retry screen was observed.

15.why: The header, stepper, card layout, button styles, and help panel are identical across all 14 steps, making the design easy to learn over time.
